old_findings.note: Checked int128 operations still print as four (mul) or two (add/sub) sign-case checks over the Point struct in memory, in all 11 _checkpoint copies. In merge the operands got longer (see regressions).

regressions.issue: The write of the updated amount to mem[192] is dropped and the new amount is forwarded as int128(int128(_18) + int128(mem[192])) into each of the 8 sign-case lines that read it (1 line before). mem[192] now means the old amount. merge grows 1.6% while the sibling functions shrink 8-10%. Consistent and same values.
regressions.rule: When a memory word is overwritten with a computed value that is read several times later, keep the write and the reads (or bind the value to a variable) rather than forwarding the compound expression into every read.

improvements: Dead scratch and struct writes dropped in withdraw, deposit_for, increase_amount, create_lock(_for) (mapping-key 'mem[0]/mem[32]' pairs, zeroed Point structs, unread locked copies); words read later are kept. Token transferFrom/transfer results read as ext_call.return_data[0] and the 'caller is not owner nor approved' revert decoded. tokenURI: constant SVG fragments are now single string-literal copies, 6 copy loops fewer (whiles 33 -> 27). merge addresses its local structs as mem[64] + K instead of _457/_467/_468. Text 11% smaller. P6 1 -> 0.
notes: Diff of 1.7k lines over 9 functions. In each function I checked that every dropped memory write is unread afterwards, including reads through join addresses (mem[_34 + 64] with _34 in {576, 704}). In merge: the unlock-time update (if _16: mem[224] = _16) and locked[_to] writes are present; old_locked.end is written before the update; old/new amounts are used where the source uses them. tokenURI's removed loops copied constant strings, and the 3 source loops (toString x2, Base64) remain.
summary: No semantic regression; dead memory writes and constant-string copy loops are gone (text 11% smaller). In merge, forwarding the updated lock amount makes 8 checkpoint lines longer.
